facts.claim: Circuits of bounded depth built from AND, OR, NOT and counting-mod-p gates need a huge number of gates to count mod a different prime q
facts.answer: for primes p ≠ q, any such circuit of depth d computing MOD_q on n inputs has size at least exponential in a power of n (the bound is written out in full)

levels.kids: A machine made of tiny switches that counts in groups of p cannot count in groups of a different prime q unless it is huge. A computer checked every step of this proof from 1987.
levels.everyone: Shallow circuits of AND, OR, NOT and mod p counting gates need exponentially many gates to count mod q, for any two different primes p and q (Razborov and Smolensky, 1987). Lean checked every step. It also proved that one published course version assumes things that can only all hold when its bound is zero.
levels.technical: HHH.MODq_AC0p_size_ge (Razborov 1987, Smolensky 1987): for primes p ≠ q, a depth-d AC0[p] circuit on n + (q − 1) inputs computing MOD_q, with n ≥ 16q + 32, has size at least 2^ℓ*(p,d,n) / (2^q · 8q(n+1)(n+2)), and ℓ* grows like n^(1/(2d)). HHH.quantitative_hyps_force_delta_zero shows the course version is vacuous.

facts.proof: Lean theorem HHH.MODq_AC0p_size_ge (known-results/razborov-smolensky/ in lean-proofs, its own pinned Lean and Mathlib; re-run it with its check.sh); 0 sorry, and it rests only on Lean's standard axioms.
facts.notProven: This is a machine-checked formalization of the known 1987 Razborov-Smolensky theorem: not new math, and not P vs NP.

facts.claim: The algebrization barrier: there is an oracle, with a low-degree extension over every finite field, relative to which NP is not in P
facts.answer: Aaronson and Wigderson Theorem 5.3: an oracle A and its degree-2 extensions over every GF(x) with NP^A not contained in P^Ã

levels.kids: A hidden box keeps a secret, and you may ask it questions, even math questions. In 2009 two scientists showed that with few questions the box can always keep its secret, so one popular trick can never settle a famous puzzle about fast computers. A computer checked every step.

Lean checked their construction for every finite field.

facts.claim: Formula lower bounds: Subbotovskaya's shrinkage, Khrapchenko's bound for parity, and Andreev's function needing large formulas
facts.answer: Khrapchenko: edges(A,B)² ≤ size × |A| × |B|; Andreev: (2^r − 2)/(4r) − 1 ≤ (r/2^r)^(3/2) × formula size

levels.kids: A formula is a recipe of ANDs and ORs. Some jobs need very long recipes. A computer checked, step by step, old proofs from 1961, 1971 and 1987 that certain jobs need long recipes.
levels.everyone: Subbotovskaya (1961) showed that fixing random inputs shrinks formulas fast, Khrapchenko (1971) that XOR on n inputs needs size about n squared, and Andreev (1987) built a function that needs much larger formulas; the Lean bound for it says something only from r = 5 up. Lean checked all of them.
